title: Curiosity and Inquiry
before:
Curiosity and inquiry spark imagination and inspire a love of learning. Encouraging children to explore, ask questions, seek answers, and express themselves ignites the innate curiosity in all children. Wonder aloud, discover natural interest, ask open-ended questions, and above all, let kids be kids.

Maine’s Science Academic Standards:

  • Maine Learning Results: Science & Engineering aka NGSS [begins on p93]. Science is a way of knowing about the world that enables people to both engage in the construction of knew knowledge and to use information to achieve desired ends. 
    • Elementary Science & Engineering standards
    • Next Generation Science Standards (NGSS) This is a searchable site by keyword, grade, practice, crosscutting concept or disciplinary core idea.
  • Multi-State Alternate Assessment (MSAA) Extended Performance Expectations. The Extended Science Expectations [EPEs] are Maine’s alternate achievement standards in science.  These standards are derived from the Next Generation Science Standards, reduced in complexity and deconstructed into smaller, more accessible steps for students with the most significant cognitive disabilities.  The EPEs are the building blocks of Maine’s alternate assessment in science, the MSAA Science.
    • Grade 5
    • Grade 8
    • High School
  • Maine's Early Learning and Development Standards (MELDS) These guidelines direct State and local early care and education practitioners’ efforts to improve early childhood professional practice and programs for children from age three through their entrance into kindergarten. The science MELDS [begin on p83] were modeled and developed to align to NGSS.

notes: 1 section header — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Rebuild the heading outline
decisions.why: 1 heading sits at a level the page never opens — "Maine’s Science Academic Standards:" is an h3 with no h2 above it, so it is neither announced nor styled as the sub-section it is. Each heading moves to one level below whatever encloses it.

decisions.label: Turn the headings into section headers
decisions.why: 1 heading is plain text where every other page uses a section header, so the page reads as one continuous wall instead of parts.

decisions.label: Tag a document link with the format it opens
decisions.why: 4 links on this page open a file — 3 Word, 1 PDF — and say nothing about it, while others in the same list carry a tag because their author typed one. The format is read from the file name, so the list stops being half-labelled. No link text changes.

decisions.label: Jumbotron callouts become notes
decisions.why: 1 callout is built as a Bootstrap jumbotron, which the component list replaced with dc-note and which Bootstrap itself removed in version 5. Same content, the site's own callout.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 3 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 1 description begins with a small letter, because it used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
